mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.1% indicates an accommodative monetary policy environment that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 7.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger risk-off sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 7.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous GDP growth above 2% annualized (GDPC1) and declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals economic weakening that reduces corporate earnings expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 > 2.0% and INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: A late-cycle expansion regime (UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS > 135000) indicates overvaluation and impending policy tightening, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days due to reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS > 135000.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 95 (index 2017=100) indicates weakening manufacturing activity that reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 95.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL below 230 (base 1982-1984=100) indicates low inflationary pressure that supports continued accommodative monetary policy, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL < 230.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 900 (thousands of units) indicate robust consumer demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of sustained economic expansion and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances when HOUST > 900.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 235 (base 1982-1984=100) signals rising inflation that may prompt monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 235.
